items.text: Points of Top(X,G)
\text{fibre functors } F\mapsto F_x\ (x\in X)\ \text{on } \operatorname{Top}(X,G)\ \text{(forget the } G\text{-action)}:\ \text{a conservative family}
x'=g\cdot x\ \Longrightarrow\ \varepsilon_x\simeq\varepsilon_{x'}
X\ \text{sober}:\quad \pi_0(\text{points of }\operatorname{Top}(X,G))=X/G,\qquad \operatorname{Isom}(x,x')=\{g\in G:\ gx=x'\}
Category of points: specialization in $X$ combined with the action of $G$; topology on isomorphism classes: quotient topology of $X/G$.
X=\mathrm{pt}:\quad \operatorname{Top}(\mathrm{pt},G)=BG,\qquad G\to G'\ \leadsto\ BG\to BG'
Topoi $\widehat C$
$C$ small; $\widehat C=$ category of contravariant functors $C\to\mathbf{Sets}$.
\Gamma(F)=\operatorname{Hom}(e,F)=\varprojlim_{C^\circ}F
F\ \text{abelian group object}\ (C^\circ\to\mathbf{Ab}):\quad H^i(\widehat C,F)=R^i\Gamma(F)=\varprojlim{}^iF
Functor $u\colon C\to C'$.
u^*\colon \widehat{C'}\to\widehat C,\qquad u^*(F')=F'\circ u
$u^*$ commutes with all limits (direct and inverse): computed termwise.
u^*\ \dashv\ u_*\colon \widehat C\to\widehat{C'},\qquad u\ \text{defines a morphism of topoi } \widehat C\to\widehat{C'}
u_!\ \dashv\ u^*\ \dashv\ u_*
$u^*$ commutes with arbitrary inverse limits $\iff$ $u^*$ has a left adjoint $u_!$ (“lower shriek”).
Example: $C'=\Delta$, $C=\Delta_{\le n}$ (finite nonempty ordered sets of cardinal $\le n+1$):

\widehat{\Delta}=\text{simplicial sets},\quad \widehat{\Delta_{\le n}}=\text{$n$-truncated simplicial sets};\qquad u_!=\operatorname{sk}_n\ \dashv\ u^*=\operatorname{tr}_n\ \dashv\ u_*=\operatorname{cosk}_n
$G\colon \widehat C\to\mathbf{Sets}$ has a left adjoint iff it commutes with arbitrary inverse limits; a right adjoint iff it commutes with arbitrary direct limits.
u_!\ \dashv\ u^*\ \dashv\ u_*\ \dashv\ u^!
$u_!$ exists iff $u^*$ commutes with all inverse limits; $u^!$ exists iff $u_*$ commutes with all limits.
If $u_!$ is also left exact: $u_!=v^*$ for a morphism of topoi $v$ in the opposite direction, and $u^*=v_*$.
u_!\ \text{left exact}\iff u\ \text{flat}\ \Longrightarrow\ u_!=w^*,\quad w\colon \widehat{C'}\to\widehat C
This holds when $C,C'$ have finite inverse limits and $u$ is left exact.
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(C,C')\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{top}}(\widehat C,\widehat{C'})\quad\text{a 2-functor, fully faithful}
The morphisms with $u^*$ commuting with arbitrary inverse limits come (almost) from functors, if $C,C'$ are Karoubi-closed (images of projectors exist).
Final and initial topoi
f^*\colon \mathbf{Sets}\to\mathcal E,\quad f^*(\mathrm{pt})=e\ (\text{final}),\qquad f^*(I)=\coprod_I e
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathcal E,\mathbf{Sets})\simeq \text{point category}
The topos of sets is final: one and only one morphism $f_{\mathcal E}\colon\mathcal E\to\mathrm{pt}$.
\operatorname{Hom}(\mathrm{pt},f_*X)=\operatorname{Hom}(f^*\mathrm{pt},X)=\operatorname{Hom}(e,X)=\Gamma(X)
\Gamma=f_{\mathcal E*}\quad(\text{sections = direct image to the point})
Cohomology as derived functors of $f_*$ for $f\colon\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$ (relative situation).
$f^*\colon I\mapsto\coprod_I e$ commutes with arbitrary products $\iff$ $\mathcal E$ locally connected (every object is a sum of connected objects).
\coprod_{\prod_\alpha I_\alpha}e\ \longrightarrow\ \prod_\alpha\Bigl(\coprod_{I_\alpha}e\Bigr)\quad\text{an isomorphism}
Topoi $\widehat C$: locally connected and “totally disconnected”; share all exactness properties of $\mathbf{Sets}$ (infinite limits included).
\operatorname{Top}(\varnothing)=\text{the one-object category},\qquad \varnothing\ \text{is the initial topos}
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathcal E,\operatorname{Top}(\varnothing))\neq\varnothing\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathcal E\ \text{empty}\qquad (\text{initial object strictly initial})
Classifying topos of a group object
$G$ a group object of a topos $\mathcal E$; $B_{\mathcal E}G$: objects of $\mathcal E$ on which $G$ acts.
G\to G'\ \leadsto\ B_{\mathcal E}G\to B_{\mathcal E}G',\qquad f^*:\ X\ (G'\text{-action})\mapsto X\ (G\text{-action via } G\to G')
Direct sums of topoi
\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(\coprod_i X_i,Z\bigr)=\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_i,Z)
$\coprod X_i$: disjoint union, each $X_i$ open with its own topology.
